title: At four and a half months, a short screen fooled infants and a short cup did not
summary: Baillargeon and Wang report that 4.5-month-olds noticed a tall object hiding behind a half-height screen, and did not notice the same trick inside a cup.
body: Their 2002 review recounts Hespos and Baillargeon's screen test. A cylinder with a knob was lowered until only the knob remained. Behind an occluder that was only half the cylinder's height, 4.5-month-olds looked longer than they did behind a tall enough occluder. Run the identical contrast by lowering the cylinder into a cup, and that age group did not give the longer look. The authors read this as height being available for hiding-behind, and not yet for hiding-inside. The report is about those infants. It is not a checklist.

sources.title: Event categorization in infancy
sources.author: Renée Baillargeon and Su-hua Wang
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Trends in Cognitive Sciences review, 1 February 2002, PMC4215955. Paraphrase of the 4.5-month occlusion-versus-containment height result.
